newsitem.title: FRANCE: No delay to French SNCF rail reform - Pons.
newsitem.headline: No delay to French SNCF rail reform - Pons.

text.p: French Transport Minister Bernard Pons said on Thursday there was no question of delaying reform of the SNCF state railways in the face of a strike call by one of the big trade unions opposed to the overhaul.
"The reform will be carried out because it is necessary for the SNCF, the railworkers, and in my mind, the whole country," Pons said.
Asked if the government was prepared to further delay the reform bill, already put on hold in November as he sought to appease unions, Pons told Europe 1 radio, "absolutely not".
"Every month that passes costs a billion-and-a-half. We cannot go on like that. We have to try to haul the SNCF out of this downward spiral," he said.

"Right now the debate is over. This has gone on for a year. I have met the unions on several occasions. Eight out of eight of them say the situation cannot carry on. Six out of the eight accept the reform," he added.
Six unions are ready to back a reform which would create a state company to take over 134.2 billion francs ($24.87 billion) of SNCF debts totalling 208 billion.
The governent, keen to narrow union disquiet, recently decided to raise the amount of debt being taken off the SNCF's hands from 125 billion francs.

This new state company, likely to be called France Rail, would become owner of the infrastructure and charge the SNCF, which would continue as railways operator and maintain the infrastructure, fees for use of the network.
But the split is opposed by the Communist-led CGT union and the Socialist CFDT on the grounds that it amounts to a break-up and a precursor to opening France's railways to competition.

With an echo of last year's crippling rail strike over a now defunct government plan to abolish early retirement for rail staff, the CFDT has called for a strike to coincide with the reform bill's introduction in the Senate on January 21.
But the CFDT failed in a meeting on Wednesday to win backing from other unions, most notably the larger CGT faction, which is assessing its own alternatives. ($1=5.395 French Franc)
